BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORD

T. R. Smith, comp.  Poetica Erotica: Rare and Curious Amatory Verse.  1921–22.

Songs from “The Tragedy of Valentinian”

By Francis Beaumont (1584–1616) and John Fletcher (1579–1625)

 
(From Act II. Scene IV.)
I.
N
OW
 the lusty spring is seen;

  Golden yellow, gaudy blue,

Daintily invite the view.

  Every where, on every green,

Roses blushing as they blow,
        5

  And enticing men to pull;

Lilies whiter than the snow,

  Woodbines of sweet honey full:

    All love’s emblems, and all cry,

    “Ladies, if not pluck’d, we die.”
        10

 

Yet the lusty spring hath staid;

  Blushing red, and purest white,

  Daintily to love invite

Every woman, every maid,

Cherries kissing as they grow,
        15

  And inviting men to taste;

Apples even ripe below.

  Winding gently to the waist:

    All love’s emblems, and all cry,

    “Ladies, if not pluck’d, we die.”
        20

 

II.
H
EAR
 ye, ladies that despise

  What the mighty Love has done;

Fear examples, and be wise:

  Fair 
Calisto
 was a nun;

Leda,
 sailing on the stream
        25

  To deceive the hopes of man,

Love accounting but a dream,

  Doted on a silver swan;

Danae
 in a brazen tower,

  Where no love was, loved a shower.
        30

 

Hear ye, ladies that are coy,

  What the mighty Love can do;

Fear the fierceness of the boy:

  The chaste moon he makes to woo;

Vesta
 kindling holy fires,
        35

  Circled round about with spies,

Never dreaming loose desires,

  Doting at the altar dies;

    
Ilion
 in a short hour higher

    He can build, and once more fire.
        40
